No code is submitted. The audited object is Ta-Shma’s complete-output `s`-wide lift. Start with labels `z_v∈F_2^r`, `v∈[N_1]`; an outer undirected `(N_1,D_1,λ_1)` rotation graph; and an inner `(D_1^s,D_2,λ_2)` graph. Enumerate every starting state and every `t`-step instruction string. The resulting multiset has exactly

`M=N_1 D_1^s D_2^t`

columns, each the XOR of the `t+1` outer labels visited by the corresponding path. Ta-Shma’s Theorem 4.1 bounds its absolute bias by

`Q^floor(t/s)`, where
`Q=λ_2^s+sλ_2^(s-1)+s^2(λ_2^(s-3)+ζ)`,

under `ε_0+2β+2λ_1≤λ_2^2`. The proved obstruction below shows that a contracting instance with outer-label span at least 65 has `M≥2^30+2^24`; hence the complete-output component cannot fit the target length.

Ta-Shma’s theorem supplies a two-sided absolute-bias certificate, stronger than the campaign’s one-sided requirement.
A `τ`-balanced core contains no all-one word. Adjoining the all-one word therefore adds exactly one dimension and preserves minimum distance by complementing every core word.
The obstruction bounds only the published complete-output certificate. It makes no minimum-distance claim for a new code and does not exclude a new one-sided or sparse-path proof.
explicitness_audit: The complete path cloud is deterministically indexed by `(v,w,i_0,…,i_{t-1})∈[N_1]×[D_1]^s×[D_2]^t`.
Given deterministic rotation maps and base labels, every output column is computed without search or randomness.
Duplicate path labels must remain with their multiplicities: deduplication changes the uniform distribution certified by the theorem.
A specially chosen puncture set, weighted path family, or sparse subfamily requires a new simultaneous all-character proof.

generator_matrix.algorithm: For a fully specified audited instance, enumerate `(v,w,i_0,…,i_{t-1})` lexicographically. Apply the deterministic Ta-Shma PATH recursion, XOR the `t+1` visited labels `z_v`, and emit the resulting `r` bits as one column of the transposed generator matrix. If auditing the standard all-one augmentation, append a final row containing one in every column. No target-meeting instance is claimed.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(M[t(T_G+T_H)+r(t+1)+s])` bit operations for `M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t`, where `T_G,T_H` bound one rotation-map evaluation.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `M` path indices. Each requires `t` outer/inner rotation steps and `t+1` XORs of `r`-bit labels, after which all `rM` output entries are emitted. Thus explicit polynomial-time rotation maps give polynomial total time in the raw matrix size, matching its output-size lower bound. The obstruction is therefore parameter-theoretic, not an explicitness failure.

proof_markdown:
## Sharpened finite obstruction

Let `r` be the span dimension of the `N_1` outer labels in a complete-output instance of [Ta-Shma’s Theorem 4.1](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Papers/T.STOC17.pdf). If the theorem’s displayed bound is below one and `r≥65`, then

`M=N_1D_1^sD_2^t ≥ 2^30+2^24`.

Consequently no complete-output specialization of length at most `2^30` has balanced rank at least 65. After the standard all-one augmentation, this route has target dimension at most 65.

### 1. Rank and the graph trace bound

Every amplified label is an XOR of visited outer labels, so amplification cannot increase their span. Hence `N_1≥r≥65`.

Let `P` be the normalized adjacency matrix of an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph on `m` vertices. Write `P_uv=a_uv/D`, where the integral symmetric port multiplicities have row sum `D`. Then

`tr(P^2)=D^-2 Σ_{u,v}a_uv^2 ≥ D^-2 Σ_{u,v}a_uv=m/D`.

If every nonconstant eigenvalue has absolute value at most `λ`, spectral decomposition gives

`tr(P^2)≤1+(m-1)λ^2`.

Therefore

`D≥m/[1+(m-1)λ^2]`.

### 2. What contraction forces

Write

`Q=λ_2^s+sλ_2^(s-1)+s^2(λ_2^(s-3)+ζ)`.

If `t<s`, the theorem’s exponent `floor(t/s)` is zero and its bound is one. For `s≤3`, the term `s^2λ_2^(s-3)` is at least one for every positive admissible spectral upper bound; an actual zero eigenvalue may be replaced by any positive upper bound. Thus a subunit certificate requires `t≥s`, `s≥4`, and `Q<1`.

Since `ζ≥0`, contraction gives

`s^2λ_2^(s-3)<1`, hence `λ_2^2<s^(-4/(s-3))`.

The compatibility hypothesis and nonnegativity of `ε_0,β` give `2λ_1≤λ_2^2`. Consequently

`λ_1^2<a_s`, where `a_s=(1/4)s^(-8/(s-3))`.

### 3. Exact finite degree split

For `4≤s≤11`, define

`d_s=(65,64,58,50,42,36,31,27)`.

If `D_1≤d_s-1`, monotonicity of `(m-D)/(D(m-1))` in `m≥65` and `D≤d_s-1` makes the trace lower bound at least

`b_s=(1/4096,1/2016,1/456,1/196,3/328,3/224,7/384,3/128)`.

The inequality `b_s≥a_s` is equivalent to `(4b_s)^(s-3)s^8≥1`. In order of `s=4,…,11`, the exact values are

`64`, `390625/254016`, `1679616/1481544`, `1`, `4076863488/3707398432`, `31381059609/30840979456`, `82354300000000/75144747810816`, and `1406408618241/1099511627776`.

All are at least one, contradicting `λ_1^2<a_s`. Hence `D_1≥d_s`. The resulting lower bounds `65d_s^s` are respectively

`1,160,290,625`, `69,793,218,560`, `2,474,465,015,360`, `50,781,250,000,000`, `629,372,379,767,040`, `6,601,397,183,447,040`, `53,275,838,653,752,065`, and `361,338,936,826,108,995`.

Each exceeds `2^30+2^24`.

For `s≥12`, one has `a_s<1/4`. If `D_1≤3`, the trace bound at `N_1≥65` gives

`λ_1^2≥(65-3)/(3·64)=31/96>1/4`,

a contradiction. Thus `D_1≥4`, and

`M≥65·4^s≥65·4^12=2^30+2^24=1,090,519,040`.

This completes the rank-length proof.

### 4. Exact-length adjustments

The lower bound exceeds the target length by `2^24`. Repetition cannot decrease length. Deduplication changes the certified path distribution.

Suppose a raw `B_0`-biased multiset of length `M>N` is blindly punctured to `N`. Its remaining absolute signed sum is bounded only by

`B_0M+(M-N)`.

To certify bias at most `τ`, it is necessary that `M-N≤τN=2^21`, or `M≤2^30+2^21`. But the proved lower bound is `2^30+2^24`, larger by `14,680,064`. Thus theorem-only puncturing also fails.

### 5. The paper’s instantiated schedules

The near-optimal Section 5 branch requires `α≤1/100` and

`α^3/(2log_2(1/α))≥1/log_2(1/τ)=1/9`.

The left side is less than `1/12,000,000`, so this branch is unavailable.

The Section 3 fallback fixes `ε_0=4/5`, `β=1/100`, and `ζ=41/50+2λ<9/10`. Since `512·41^31>50^31`, one has `ζ^31>1/512`; therefore `t=2ceil(log_ζ(1/512))≥64`. Its complete path enumeration also exceeds the coordinate budget.

The obstruction is confined to the published complete-output theorem and its displayed certificates. A deterministic sparse or weighted path family with a new all-character proof remains open.

proof_steps.statement: Every contracting Theorem 4.1 instance obeys the stated outer spectral upper bound.

proof_steps.proof: The exact `s=4,…,11` table forces degrees `65,64,58,50,42,36,31,27`; for `s≥12`, the trace inequality forces `D_1≥4`. All cases give `M≥65·4^12=2^30+2^24`.

proof_steps.proof: A balanced core from the direct theorem has rank at most 64. Since it excludes the all-one vector, the standard all-one augmentation adds exactly one dimension.

research_direction: Ta-Shma bias amplification with every constant exposed
theorem_statement: For every complete-output application of Ta-Shma’s STOC 2017 Theorem 4.1, if the outer labels span at least 65 binary dimensions and the displayed bias certificate is below one, then the raw output length is at least `2^30+2^24=1,090,519,040`. Hence no such exact-length lift has balanced rank at least 65; even the standard all-one augmentation has dimension at most 65, and blind puncturing based only on the theorem’s absolute-bias bound cannot meet the immutable target.
title: A rank-64 ceiling for complete-output Ta-Shma amplification at length 2^30
